title: Put it together: decomposition
idea: LOOP: mix recall across this unit - spot too-big tasks, name sub-jobs, find repeats. No code.

options: Breaking a big problem into smaller sub-problems
exercises.explanation: Decomposition is splitting a big task into smaller, solvable jobs. It's the heart of this unit.

exercises.prompt: A task is 'print one word'. Should you split it?
options: No - it's a single step, already small enough
exercises.explanation: Tiny one-step tasks don't need splitting. Split when there are several jobs or a repeat.

exercises.prompt: Which are signs a task should be SPLIT? (Pick all.)
options: It fits in one short step
exercises.explanation: Several jobs or a repeated job both call for a split. A single short action does not.

exercises.prompt: Order the sub-jobs of 'take an order, total it, print the receipt'.
exercises.explanation: Take, total, print - in that order. Decomposition keeps the jobs in a sensible sequence.

exercises.prompt: 'Show the banner at the top and bottom.' The banner job...
options: repeats, so it's worth naming once
exercises.explanation: The banner repeats top and bottom. A repeated job is the natural thing to name and reuse.

exercises.prompt: Match each sub-job to its tool (review).
exercises.explanation: Each named sub-job maps to a familiar tool. Naming jobs then picking tools is the plan.

exercises.prompt: Why give each sub-job a clear name?
options: So the plan reads clearly and each job is easy to find and fix
exercises.explanation: Clear names make the plan readable and the jobs fixable. Vague names waste that chance.

exercises.prompt: Decomposition is the same core skill you first met as 'order 2 to 3 steps', now deeper.
exercises.explanation: Yes - one pillar, revisited and deepened into named, reusable sub-jobs.

exercises.prompt: A big task feels scary. Decomposition helps because...
options: it becomes many small, familiar jobs you can solve one by one
exercises.explanation: Small familiar jobs replace one big unknown. That's why splitting makes hard problems doable.

exercises.prompt: You've learned to spot and name sub-jobs. The next step in this lap is...
options: giving a reusable sub-job a name you can call - then writing it as code
exercises.explanation: Next: name a reusable sub-plan (Unit 70), then write it as real runnable code (Unit 71). Great planning foundation!
